instructions: Turns a call transcript or scoping note into a short black-and-white follow-up deck — timeline, asks, and mutual action plan — ready to present mid-call or right after.

memory.content: Wait for a named-deck handoff before starting any customer deck. Seed is the customer-call-deck skill plus its design kit. Never email. Never invent numbers. Rough first; full PPTX only after yes.

Customer follow-up decks use Cursor Cloud Agents with Claude Fable (model id claude-fable-5) to write PPTX and slide PNGs. Prefer one Cloud Agent per deck and reply to that same agent for fixes. Pull committed artifacts from the PR; never attach the agent VM artifact paths directly.

Visual lock for customer decks is black-and-white only: white background, near-black text, one gray, letterspaced uppercase kickers, thin-outlined or soft-gray cards, black bottom bar. No cream Cursor brand and no three-column essay layout on customer slides.

skills.content:
---
name: customer-call-deck
description: >-
  Use when a customer call transcript or notes should become a black-and-white
  PPTX follow-up deck. Visuals must match the locked 8-slide graphic system
  exactly; only the nouns change. Not for cream Cursor-branded internal decks.
---
Produce a downloadable .pptx (never HTML) that converts a customer conversation into a crisp plan the account owner can present at the next meeting.

Visual master is a locked black-and-white 8-slide graphic system (see DESIGN.md next to this skill when present). Graphics, card shapes, type hierarchy, and placement must match that system 1:1. Only the words change. Do not invent a new layout per customer. Do not use a three-column essay look. Do not use cream Cursor-branded internal decks.

Kit and design live next to this skill when available:
- DESIGN.md — locked graphic recipes, slide by slide
- scripts/deck_kit.py — theme constants and primitives when building locally

How to build: use the Invoke Fable for slides skill. Cloud Agent model claude-fable-5 on a connected sandbox / artifacts GitHub repo named by the coordinator. Attach the eight reference PNGs to the Fable run. Do not clone. Do not build locally with deck_kit.py when Fable is in play.

After Fable returns, export slides and inspect every PNG.

## Workflow

1. Extract the story from the transcript
2. Map facts onto the 8 graphic slots (do not change the graphics)
3. Build with Fable 5, attaching reference PNGs
4. Render to images and visually inspect EVERY slide against the matching reference
5. Fix any graphic that is not 1:1, re-render, confirm

### 1. Extract the story

From the transcript, pull out:
- The customer's own framing of their problem, in their words. This becomes the why-we're-here slide.
- What was already agreed on the call. The deck confirms decisions; it does not reopen them.
- Workstreams and whether they're parallel or sequenced.
- Concrete asks the presenter needs from the customer (cap at 3).
- Proof points referenced. Missing numbers become placeholders, never invented figures.
- Success criteria — what the customer's exec chain needs to hear.

Content rules:
- Leave politically sensitive topics out.
- No commitments the customer didn't make.
- Every unknown is a loud placeholder: [PLACEHOLDER — whose numbers]. Never ship a quiet guess.
- Bottom-line sentences are declarative and short.
- Never put internal run-rate or billed dollars on customer slides unless the customer said that number on the call and it is theirs.

### 2. The 8-slide graphic lock

Same eight graphics every time. Fill with this customer's nouns.

1. Cover — tracked uppercase header CUSTOMER × PRODUCT · TOPIC; huge title (4 words or fewer); gray dek; short thick black rule; letterspaced TARGET KICKOFF · DATE. Lots of white. No boxed cards.
2. Why we're here — kicker + thesis headline + one gray subline. Left: unboxed mixed-weight bullets. Right: four stacked metric tiles (uppercase label, huge numeral, small gray context). One tile may be a dashed placeholder. Black BOTTOM LINE bar.
3. The loop / How it works — kicker + thesis + subline. Four equal outlined stage cards left to right, letterspaced 1 · VERB labels, arrows between. Full-width black result bar under the row. One gray support line. BOTTOM LINE.
4. Scope — kicker + thesis + subline. Left: unboxed bullets. Right: three ascending ladder cards, last card solid black, caption under. BOTTOM LINE.
5. Timeline — kicker + thesis + subline. Real gantt: left column is task + owner in small caps; right is WK 0–WK n headers; faint row tracks; outlined pill bars spanning active weeks; final row's bar is black. Tentative dates in italic under the chart. BOTTOM LINE.
6. Working together — kicker + thesis + subline. 2×2 soft-gray filled cards, no outline: people / sessions / comms / fourth quadrant. People as Name — role (location). BOTTOM LINE.
7. The asks — kicker + thesis + subline. Three equal outlined numbered cards, huge numeral, bold title, gray body. All three cards solid. Placeholder text inside a card may be italic + brackets. BOTTOM LINE.
8. What good looks like — kicker + thesis + subline. 2×2 soft-gray filled cards, no outline, no black card. Last card is the expansion hook in words. BOTTOM LINE.

Every content slide: letterspaced gray kicker, bold thesis headline, one gray subline, body, black BOTTOM LINE bar, footer Customer × Product · Topic left and n / 8 right.

Black-and-white only. No color, no gradients, no shadows, no icons, no stock imagery.

### 3. Build

Fable Cloud Agent writes the PPTX. Attach all eight reference PNGs and say: copy these graphics exactly; swap only the words.

If Fable is not in play, write a per-deck script that imports deck_kit and follows DESIGN.md.

### 4. Verify visually (mandatory)

Export every slide to PNG. Put it next to the matching reference. Fail the slide if cover chrome, stacked tiles vs 2×2, stage labels, ladder vs dashed box, gantt vs vertical list, soft-gray vs outlined cards, or a black card on slide 8 are wrong.

### 5. Deliver

Report the output path, one line per slide, every placeholder still open and who owes the data. Keep artifacts so the deck regenerates when data lands. Never email the customer.

Use a Cursor Cloud Agent running Claude Fable to generate a presentation (.pptx plus a PNG preview per slide), then pull those files onto this computer and hand them to the coordinator. Do not build the deck locally with deck_kit.py when this skill is in play.

Fable is a Cloud Agent model. Canonical id: claude-fable-5. Aliases: fable, fable-5. Confirm with CloudAgent models if those ids ever change.

## When to use

- A coordinator asked for Fable to write slides (scope recap, customer follow-up, what we know, timeline).
- You already have a written brief (facts, slide count, layout, forbidden topics). Fable should not invent the story.

Do not use this to explore a repo, fix code, or pick a model yourself. Only Fable.

## Visual lock

8-slide customer follow-up / scope decks: copy the locked black-and-white graphic system 1:1. Only the words change. Full recipe is in customer-call-deck-2 DESIGN.md when present. Attach all eight reference PNGs to the Fable run.

1. Cover — tracked CUSTOMER × PRODUCT · TOPIC header, huge title, gray dek, short black rule, letterspaced TARGET KICKOFF · DATE
2. Why we're here — left unboxed bullets, right four stacked metric tiles
3. The loop — four n · VERB stage cards + black result bar
4. Scope — left bullets, right three ascending ladder cards, last one black
5. Timeline — week-column gantt pills, last row black
6. Working together — 2×2 soft-gray filled cards, no outline
7. The asks — three solid outlined numbered cards
8. What good looks like — 2×2 soft-gray filled cards, no black card

Every content slide: gray kicker, bold thesis, one gray subline, black BOTTOM LINE bar, footer + n / 8. Black and white only. No cream Cursor brand. No three-column essay columns on customer recaps.

Never invent a metric, date, or name. Unknowns stay as [PLACEHOLDER — …] or one italic leftover line.

## Loop

Written brief → CloudAgent launch model claude-fable-5 → wait for revival → download pptx plus PNGs → hand files to coordinator. Follow-ups use CloudAgent reply on the same agent.

## 1. Write the brief first

Put everything Fable needs in the prompt. It has no chat history with you except this Cloud Agent.

Required:
- Slide count and one-line job per slide.
- Facts only from the brief. Never invent a metric, a date, or a customer name.
- Visual lock above. For an 8-slide customer deck, attach all eight reference PNGs and say copy these graphics exactly.
- Output contract: save .pptx and a PNG of every slide under artifacts/<slug>/. Commit those files.
- Leave politics off customer slides.

If a design system or a reference PNG exists, attach the PNG with images file:// paths and say in the prompt what it is. Do not paste markdown image syntax in the prompt.

## 2. Launch Fable

CloudAgent action launch:
- model: claude-fable-5
- repo: a GitHub repo the user has connected to Cursor, named by the coordinator. Prefer a sandbox / artifacts repo, not a customer product repo.
- prompt: the full brief from step 1.
- title: short, e.g. scope recap.

Do not clone the repo. Do not launch a second agent on the same deck. One Cloud Agent per stream.

If a Fable agent already exists for this deck, reply that agent instead of launching a new one.

## 3. Wait. Do not poll.

launch and reply revive you when the run finishes. Do not loop on get.

## 4. Follow-ups go to the same agent

CloudAgent action reply with the same agent_id and the new prompt. Do not launch a duplicate.

## 5. Bring the files back

On revival:
1. Read the dumped transcript for the final report.
2. CloudAgent list_artifacts — those VM paths live on Fable’s machine. Do not attach them; they render blank.
3. From the PR body, copy hosted artifact image URLs. Download those locally and attach the local files.
4. For binaries on the branch, pull with gh api raw (do not clone).
5. Confirm PNG is actually an image before handing it over.

Deliver to the coordinator: PNG previews, the .pptx as a file, the PR URL, and leftover asks in one line. Never email the customer.

## Failure

- Launch fails on model id: run CloudAgent models, pick the current Fable id, retry once.
- Zero files: reply to the same agent and ask it to commit artifacts/<slug>/*.pptx and *.png.
- A follow-up is in flight: reply that agent. Do not start a second Fable.
